overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Taḥash, Tefillin Hides, and a Folded Wick
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 28a–28b
overview.hebrewSource: פְּתִילַת הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁקִּיפְּלָהּ וְלֹא הִבְהֲבָהּ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר טְמֵאָה הִיא, וְאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר טְהוֹרָה הִיא, וּמַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara derives, via a gezera shava linking 'tent' in the corpse-impurity verses to 'tent' in the Tabernacle, that only linen fully qualifies as an impurity-susceptible tent — yet other coverings, like the Tabernacle's ram-skin and taḥash-skin roofs, are drawn back in through a separate verse. This launches a long dilemma: was the mysterious taḥash animal that provided the Tabernacle's covering kosher or not, and can a non-kosher animal's hide become impure as a tent over a corpse at all? After tracing several failed derivations, Rava mi-Barnish proves it by a fortiori from goats' hair. The Gemara also pins down which materials tefillin boxes, straps, and stitching require, then Rabbi Meir describes the one-horned taḥash itself. The daf ends with a new mishna: a garment-wick folded but not yet singed — is it still susceptible to impurity, and may it be lit on Shabbat? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva disagree on both counts.

slides.title: ⛺ Deriving 'Tent' From the Tabernacle
slides.subtitle: A gezera shava, then a needed correction

nodes.content: 📜 Numbers 19:14 ('a man dies in a tent') and Exodus 40:19 ('he spread the tent over the Tabernacle') both say 'tent'
🧵 Just as the Tabernacle's tent was linen, only a linen tent transmits corpse-impurity
❓ Should the analogy also require the Tabernacle's specific twisted, six-ply threads? No — the repeated word 'tent, tent' broadens the rule beyond that detail, but not without limit
✅ Conclusion: the amplification is bounded — it establishes linen generally, not every construction detail

callout.label: Follow-up:
callout.text: A parallel question about the Tabernacle's beams (were they part of the 'Tabernacle'?) sets up Rabbi Elazar's dilemma about the animal-hide coverings.

slides.title: 🐐 Can a Non-Kosher Hide Become a Corpse-Tent?
slides.subtitle: Multiple failed derivations before a successful one

lines.speaker: R' Elazar
lines.text: Dilemma: does the hide of a non-kosher animal become impure as a tent over a corpse?

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Derive it from tzaraat's 'or in a hide' (Lev. 13:48), which includes non-kosher hide.

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: Refuted — tzaraat is more stringent, since even unwoven warp and woof threads become impure from it.

lines.speaker: Alt.
lines.text: Then derive it from sheretz impurity, which also includes non-kosher hide (Lev. 11:32).

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: Also refuted — sheretz is stringent in a different way, transmitting impurity even at a lentil-bulk.

lines.speaker: Rava mi-Barnish
lines.text: Better: an a fortiori from goats' hair! It is not susceptible to tzaraat, yet does become a corpse-tent. So non-kosher hide, which is susceptible to tzaraat, certainly becomes a corpse-tent.

callout.label: Conclusion:
callout.text: The kal vachomer from goats' hair succeeds where the direct comparisons to tzaraat and sheretz both failed.

slides.title: 📦 Rav Yosef's Rule: Kosher Hide for 'Heavenly Service'
slides.subtitle: Tracing what it actually governs, one rejected option at a time
rows: Already resolved — non-kosher hide can become a tent, so the covering needn't be kosher
Already explicit from 'that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth' — must be from what's fit to eat
Already a halakha to Moses from Sinai (the letter shin, per Abaye) — a Torah-level law already covers it
Already a separate halakha to Moses from Sinai
Only their blackness was a Sinai tradition — that they must be from a kosher animal is Rav Yosef's own teaching

slides.title: 🦄 Rabbi Meir's Taḥash: A Vanished Creature
slides.subtitle: One horn, uncertain kind, gone after the Mishkan
slides.hebrewSource: תַּחַשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה בְּרִיָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ הָיָה, וְלֹא הִכְרִיעוּ בּוֹ חֲכָמִים אִם מִין חַיָּה הוּא אִם מִין בְּהֵמָה הוּא
slides.label: The tradition:
slides.text: Rabbi Ela, citing Reish Lakish, reports that Rabbi Meir described the taḥash of Moses's time as a creature unto itself — the Sages could not determine whether it was a wild or domesticated species. It had a single horn on its forehead, appeared to Moses just in time for the Tabernacle's construction, and was then hidden away, never to be seen again. Its single horn suggests it was kosher (compare Adam's one-horned ox, Psalms 69:32), but the comparison to the one-horned keresh (a wild species) leaves the question of wild-versus-domesticated unresolved.

slides.title: 🕯️ New Mishna: A Folded but Unsinged Wick
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva disagree on two separate questions

steps.content: 1️⃣ Mishna: a cloth wick folded into shape but not yet singed — Rabbi Eliezer: impure, may not be lit; Rabbi Akiva: pure, may be lit
2️⃣ On impurity: R' Eliezer holds folding alone doesn't cancel the cloth's garment-status; R' Akiva holds it does
3️⃣ On lighting (Rav Oshaya/Rav Adda bar Ahava): the case is a cloth exactly three-by-three fingerbreadths, lit on a Festival that falls on Friday
4️⃣ Both need Rabbi Yehuda's rule (only whole vessels, not broken ones, may fuel a Festival fire) and Ulla's rule (most of the wick must be lit)
5️⃣ R' Eliezer: once part burns, what's left is a 'broken vessel' — forbidden. R' Akiva: folding already removed vessel-status, so it's just plain wood

summary.principle: A gezera shava ties corpse-tent impurity to the Tabernacle's linen tent, non-kosher hide is shown by a fortiori to share that impurity, kosher hide is required specifically for tefillin straps, and the mishna's folded wick dispute turns on whether folding alone cancels a cloth's vessel-status.

flowSteps.content: ⛺ 'Tent'-'tent' gezera shava: corpse-impurity tents, like the Tabernacle's, must be linen
🐐 Does non-kosher hide become a corpse-tent? Tzaraat and sheretz comparisons fail; a fortiori from goats' hair succeeds

columns.content: 📦 Rav Yosef: kosher hide required — ultimately, only for tefillin straps
🦄 R' Meir: the taḥash was a unique one-horned creature that then vanished

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: R' Eliezer holds folding a wick doesn't cancel its garment-status (still impure, still a 'broken vessel' once lit); R' Akiva holds folding does

quiz.q: What does the gezera shava between 'tent' in the corpse-impurity verse and 'tent' in the Tabernacle verse teach?
o: That any tent material can transmit impurity
That only a tent made of linen, like the Tabernacle's, is considered a tent for corpse-impurity purposes
That the Tabernacle itself could become impure
That tents made of beams are impure
quiz.e: The Gemara derives that just as the Tabernacle's tent covering was linen, a tent over a corpse must be linen to transmit impurity — though the amplifying repetition of 'tent, tent' extends this beyond the exact Tabernacle specifications, within limits.

quiz.q: How does Rava mi-Barnish ultimately prove that a non-kosher animal's hide becomes impure as a tent over a corpse?
o: By direct verse about non-kosher hides
By an a fortiori inference from goats' hair, which is not susceptible to tzaraat impurity yet does become impure as a corpse-tent
By citing a Mishnah explicitly
By comparing it to sheretz impurity, which the Gemara accepts without objection
quiz.e: After derivations from tzaraat and sheretz impurity were both refuted, Rava mi-Barnish succeeded with a fortiori reasoning from goats' hair, which is less susceptible than non-kosher hide yet still becomes a corpse-tent.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's conclusion, for what specific part of tefillin does Rav Yosef's rule (only kosher-animal hide for 'heavenly service') actually apply?
o: The parchment scrolls inside
The boxes (batim)
The straps (retzuot), specifically that they must come from a kosher animal (their required blackness was already a separate Sinai tradition)
The tying hair and sewing sinews
quiz.e: After the parchment, boxes, and binding materials were shown to already be governed by explicit verses or Sinai traditions, the Gemara concludes Rav Yosef's rule applies to the straps, adding the requirement that they be from a kosher animal beyond their already-known required blackness.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Meir (via Rabbi Ela and Reish Lakish), what happened to the taḥash after the Tabernacle was built?
o: It was sacrificed as an offering
It became a domesticated farm animal
It was hidden away and no longer exists, having been a unique one-horned creature that appeared to Moses only for that purpose
It was replaced by ram skins permanently
quiz.e: Rabbi Meir describes the taḥash as a unique creature with one horn, of uncertain species, that appeared to Moses just for the Tabernacle's construction and was then suppressed, never to be found again.

quiz.q: In the new mishna about a folded, unsinged garment-wick, what is the core dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva regarding lighting it on Shabbat?
o: Whether wicks may ever be lit on Shabbat
Whether folding alone removes the cloth's vessel-status — R' Eliezer says no (so once lit it becomes a forbidden 'broken vessel'), R' Akiva says yes (so it is like plain wood)
Whether the wick must be exactly three by three handbreadths
Whether only linen wicks may be used
quiz.e: Per Rav Oshaya/Rav Adda bar Ahava, the case involves a Festival falling on Friday: R' Eliezer holds folding doesn't cancel vessel-status, so partial burning leaves a forbidden broken vessel; R' Akiva holds folding does cancel it, so lighting it is like lighting plain wood.
